note: Judged by eye from output/part-identification/pair-sheets/: is the step callout on the left the same part as the claimed element on the right? Nothing but the two drawings was shown. Judged against the deterministic/one-to-one claims. A verdict is keyed to the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the crop that was judged plus the element it was claimed to be, so it stops binding exactly when the picture or the claim changes, and a different claim is unjudged rather than inherited. The previous schema keyed on cluster index, which match renumbers on every re-cut; that generation is retained unbound at history/truth-first50-870gen-unbound.json.
judgedBy: agent, reading the shipped contact sheets; ambiguous pairs re-read at single-pair resolution. Two independent blind raters on different models judged all 84 pairs with no access to features, match, answers, score or truth artifacts and no sight of each other verdicts; they agreed 84/84. The root session adjudicated the pairs where their descriptions diverged despite an agreeing verdict.

keyNote: The crop digest is truncated to 16 hex characters. That is 2^64 of collision space against at most a few thousand crops, and the labels grow with the booklet: at full length the all-359-step set projects past the 256 KiB blob-review threshold, which is a cost paid on every re-cut because a changed extraction rewrites every key.
